title: Resilience, stress experience and understanding of illness in depression
summary:
The lesson examines the connection between individual resilience in stressful everyday situations and the development of depressive symptoms. In addition, attitudes and causal attributions in connection with depressive symptoms are examined. The survey consists of a total of 12 parts. A survey lasting approximately 15 minutes is conducted once a week. Questions are asked about currently perceived symptoms, perceived resilience, current stress experiences, and individual attitudes and attributions. The aim is to examine long-term interrelationships between the individual factors and compare them with those of healthy individuals.
H1: Expectations regarding the course of depression influence the actual individual course of symptoms over time.
H2: The type of attribution of causes of depressive symptoms (biological vs. psychological) indirectly influences the actual course of depressive symptoms via expectations. Depressive individuals with biological attribution of causes show a more pessimistic view of the course of symptoms.
H3: The effect of expectations regarding the course of depression on the actual course of symptoms is moderated by the degree of self-efficacy, depending on the type of understanding of the illness.
H4: Healthy individuals experience a higher degree of controllability with regard to changes in symptoms than individuals with depression.

interventions.name: People who have a score of >13 on the Beck depression inventory revision (BDI-II) at the first measurement point are asked once a week over a period of 12 weeks about their depressive symptoms, their current stress levels, their perceived control over the illness and their understanding of depressio

Healthy individuals with a BDI-II score ≤13 at measurement point 1 are surveyed once a week over a period of 12 weeks about depressive symptoms, their current stress levels, their perceived control over the symptoms and their understanding of depression

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
for the group "depressive individuals": BDI-Score >13
for the group "healthy individuals": BDI-Score ≤13
Exclusion criteria:
schizophrenia
bipolar disorder
acute suicidality
